newsitem.title: USA: GM, union resume talks in Ohio strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, union resume talks in Ohio strike.

text.p: Negotiations between General Motors Corp's Delphi Packard Electric Systems Division and striking union members resumed Tuesday afternoon about 13 hours after the walkout began in Warren, Ohio.
GM spokeswoman Deborah Ayers said bargainers for the company and International Union of Electronic Workers Local 717 resumed talks at about 1300 EDT/1700 GMT.

About 8,200 workers struck 19 Delphi Packard Electric facilities in the Warren area early Tuesday over a number of grievances, including demands that GM guarantee that it will not unilaterally move jobs to Mexico.

The strike, the third against GM in about five weeks, could eventually force a broad shutdown of GM's North American car and truck operations, because the Warren facilities produce wiring harnesses and other electrical distribution components used in nearly all of GM's North American-built cars.

The dispute also could affect many other automakers that buy Delphi Packard Electric's products. The unit lists 34 other car and truck makers as customers, but not all of them are supplied by the Ohio plants.
In a statement, Delphi Packard Electric said it is "extremely disappointed" in the strike.

"Our main focus is on the impact this strike will have on our customers, both General Motors and non-GM. Any interruption, either actual or potential, in the chain of supply to our customers poses a great risk to the retention and ongoing expansion of our business," the GM unit said.
Local 717 officials were not immediately available for comment on the talks.
